text:
Carolina arrives off a 9-2 rout of Chicago, its fourth win in five games, and a +34 goal difference that runs ahead of its chances (our expected-goals measure of chance quality). Finishing and goaltending are doing much of the lifting, and Jordan Staal is out until early December. Seattle is 2-3-0 in its last five after a 4-3 loss to the Rangers, and without Jared McCann, Jordan Eberle has moved onto the line beside Matty Beniers and Mackie Samoskevich. Both teams have had four days off.

The numbers favor Carolina. At five on five it has taken 58% of the expected goals in its games, Seattle 45%, and our model projects 3.58 goals for the Hurricanes to 2.62 for the Kraken. Carolina's power play creates 0.9 expected goals a game to Seattle's 0.58. In net, Brandon Bussi is the projected Hurricanes starter, and he sits at -3.9 goals saved above expected this season, though he was +1.15 last year. Philipp Grubauer, projected for Seattle, is at -0.8 after a +5.35 season, and over his last five starts he is 4.8 goals worse than expected.

Watch Jackson Blake, on a nine-game point streak and at 62% to record a point, and Logan Stankoven, with 12 points in 10 games. Sebastian Aho leads our scoring odds at 35%. Our under-the-radar pick is Mark Jankowski, whose third-line shots have produced 4.5 expected goals in his last 10 games, with the Kraken allowing the ninth-most expected goals per 60. We have him at 23% to score. For Seattle, Berkly Catton carries an eight-game point streak.
